title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #188 review (backend-weekly-impulse-screen1-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #188 (backend-weekly-impulse-screen1-followups), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. PR #188 itself was accepted -- this finding is pre-existing (predates PR #188, missed by earlier grep sweeps for stale Tide/Screen-1 wording) and out of scope for PR #188's own diff, so it didn't block it.

checklist.step: frontend/src/features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts's valueZoneHelp.elderContext (around line 583) still says "This exact EMA13/EMA26 pair already drives the Tide (Screen 1), the Impulse System gate, and the Elder-Ray baseline elsewhere on this page (docs/Analyse.md §2-4)" -- this is stale and now factually wrong: per the `backend-weekly-impulse-screen1` methodology correction (and the already-corrected `ema26Help.elderContext` right below it in the same file, which explicitly says EMA(26) 'no longer feeds the Tide directly'), Tide/Screen 1 is driven by the weekly Impulse System color (weekly EMA(13) direction + weekly MACD-Histogram direction), not by the EMA13/EMA26 level pair. This text is user-facing (rendered via the `MetricHelp` affordance on the price chart's Value Zone legend entry, `PriceChart.tsx` line ~1809), so it's more visible than the two internal JSDoc comments PR #188 itself fixed. Reword to match `ema26Help`'s corrected framing -- e.g. that EMA13/EMA26 still feed the Impulse System's daily gate indirectly (EMA(13) is one of the two Impulse inputs; EMA(26) is MACD's slower input) and the Elder-Ray baseline, but no longer drive the Tide/Screen 1 decision itself.

decisions.decision: Reworded valueZoneHelp.elderContext to state EMA(13)/EMA(26) no longer drive the Tide/Screen 1 directly (now the weekly Impulse System color), but that EMA(13) still feeds the daily Impulse System gate as one of its two inputs and both still feed the Elder-Ray baseline -- mirroring ema26Help.elderContext's corrected framing rather than dropping the Impulse-System mention entirely.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's own suggested rewording kept an indirect Impulse System connection (EMA(13) is one of the two daily Impulse inputs) rather than removing all mention of it, which matches how ema26Help.elderContext (a few lines above) already frames the same pair post-correction -- keeping the two elderContext strings consistent in how they describe the same underlying fact was preferred over independently wording each one. No existing test asserted the stale copy verbatim, so no test needed updating beyond re-running the suite to confirm nothing else depended on it.

decisions.decision: Narrowed valueZoneHelp.elderContext's Elder-Ray reference to EMA(13) only ('EMA(13) alone is still the baseline Elder-Ray measures Bull/Bear Power against'), splitting the daily-Impulse-gate clause into EMA(13) feeding the gate directly and EMA(26) feeding that same gate's MACD-Histogram half -- rather than dropping EMA(26) from the sentence entirely.
decisions.rationale: pr-reviewer's needs_work finding on PR #197 was correct: app/indicators/elder_ray.py's bull_power/bear_power only ever use ema_13, never ema_26 (docs/Analyse.md #4 row 5 confirms 'Elder-Ray (Bull/Bear Power) | Daily | EMA 13'), matching the already-correct sibling ema13Help.elderContext a few lines above. Kept EMA(26)'s genuinely accurate connection (it feeds the daily Impulse gate's MACD-Histogram input) rather than removing EMA(26) from the sentence altogether, since deleting it would lose real, correct information the reviewer explicitly said to keep. No test asserted the exact old wording verbatim, so no test file needed a corresponding edit -- confirmed by grep across frontend/src and frontend/tests before/after.

comments.summary: valueZoneHelp.elderContext's new copy claims "this pair [EMA(13)/EMA(26)] still feeds ... the Elder-Ray baseline" -- factually wrong for EMA(26): app/indicators/elder_ray.py's bull_power/bear_power only ever take ema_13 (high - ema_13, low - ema_13), never EMA(26), per docs/Analyse.md §4 row 5 ("Elder-Ray (Bull/Bear Power) | Daily | EMA 13") and the correctly-worded sibling ema13Help.elderContext a few lines above in the same file ("Also the baseline Elder-Ray measures Bull/Bear Power against" -- EMA13 only, no EMA26 mention). Predates this PR (the old stale text and the checklist item's own suggested rewording both made the same over-broad claim), but since this PR's whole purpose is fixing inaccurate copy in this exact sentence, the Elder-Ray half needs narrowing to EMA(13) only (the Impulse-gate half of the same sentence is accurate as written -- EMA(26) does feed daily MACD-Histogram, the Impulse System's second input).

review.notes: git diff main...task/backend-weekly-impulse-screen1-followups-followups --stat confirmed only metricHelpContent.ts (the valueZoneHelp.elderContext string) plus task-JSON bookkeeping changed -- no app logic. Backend: pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90 -- 920 passed, 99.94% coverage. Frontend: vitest run --coverage -- 684 passed / 1 failed (PortfolioPage.test.tsx 'adds a new position end to end', a 5000ms timeout under coverage-instrumentation CPU load); confirmed pre-existing environmental flake unrelated to this PR (passes standalone 3/3 reruns, zero relation to the changed file, already documented as this same flake in prior reviews e.g. docs/tasks/done/backend-indicator-rsi.json's pr_decision.notes) -- not blocking. tsc -b --noEmit, eslint ., backend ruff check app/, mypy all clean. Real browser walkthrough: started backend (FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture) + frontend dev server, loaded /stocks/AAPL, opened the Value Zone MetricHelp tooltip via a Playwright script (no MCP browser tools available this session) -- new copy renders correctly, zero console errors, zero failed requests. make e2e: all 16 Playwright specs passed. Broad grep sweep across frontend/src for any other remaining stale Tide/Screen-1 copy from the PR #187 methodology change found nothing else stale -- every other reference (tideHelp, ema13Help, ema26Help, tideRegionHelp, ScreensPanel.tsx, PriceChart.tsx, signalExplanation.ts, methodologyContent.ts, api/types.ts) already correctly frames Screen 1 as the weekly Impulse System color. One blocking finding (Elder-Ray/EMA26 misattribution, posted inline on the PR) sends this back to implementing rather than accepted.
